chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Rifah ibn Musa from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who dies and has no heir and no mawla (client/kin), he said: 'He is among the people of this verse: They ask you about the spoils of war (al-Anfal).'

key_terms.اَلْأَنْفال: Al-Anfal (spoils of war/gains, referring to Surah 8:1)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the estate of a person who dies with no heirs and no mawla in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the estate of a person with no heirs or mawla to the concept of *al-Anfal* mentioned in Surah Al-Anfal, establishing that the entire property reverts to the Imam (or the state treasury) as divine surplus. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the distribution of *Ghanimah* or public treasury assets when no specific heirs exist, distinguishing it from general inheritance. The reference to 'They ask you' highlights the Quranic context where *al-Anfal* refers to surplus wealth under the Imam's authority, reinforcing the Imam's role as the ultimate distributor of such assets.
